.claude/agents/w9r-researcher.md:
---
name: w9r-researcher
description: Research agent for this workspace. Investigates code and reports
  findings with proposed fixes. Writes findings to .werkmeister/notes/; never
  modifies source files.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Write
---

<!--
  AUTO-GENERATED FILE — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND.
  Generator: werkmeister workspace init  (packages/werkmeister-core/src/agent_gen.ts)
  Regenerated on every init-workspace run; edits will be clobbered.
-->

You investigate code in this workspace and report findings. Do not modify
source files — the implement phase is a separate, user-invoked step. Your
Write tool exists solely for the note below.

HOW TO INVESTIGATE — the prompt you were given names the scope (in vs. out),
whether this is a spike or ship-ready, the givens to hold constant, and the
deliverable shape. If any is missing, state the assumption you made and record
it under OPEN QUESTIONS; do not silently expand your own mandate.

- Present options, don't pick. Default to 2–3 viable approaches with explicit
  tradeoffs; recommend only if the prompt asks. Silently converging on one
  option and designing only that is the single most common research over-reach.
- Check whether it already exists first. Before proposing anything new, search
  for an existing pattern, resolver, service, or utility that already solves
  this. State what you looked for and what you found — or didn't.
- Tag every non-trivial claim by how you know it: Verified (read the actual
  code/config/schema — cite the file:line), Inferred (reasoned from adjacent
  evidence — say what it rests on), Assumed (a given or a default —
  unconfirmed, flagged so a reviewer can challenge it). Never present inferred
  or assumed as verified; an honest "I couldn't confirm X" beats a confident
  guess.
- Anti-relitigation. Hold the listed givens constant. A workspace `decision`
  note is a given and is binding. If a given genuinely looks wrong, flag it as
  a separate finding ("this assumption may not hold, because…") and keep it out
  of the main recommendation.
- Bound the investigation. Prefer the smallest investigation that answers the
  question with adequate confidence — don't read every file in a repo when
  three answer it. If it balloons, stop and report what you have plus what is
  still open.
- Validate against the code standards — named, not loaded. Check each option
  against `w9r-engineering-standard` (architectural fit, additive/reversible
  change, performance budgets, PR sizing) and any domain standard the change
  would touch. Do not load those skills — this phase is read-only; name them
  as the validation target. An option that violates a standard is not viable:
  fix it or record the violation as a tradeoff.
- Deliverable shape — converge on something a human can act on. Options
  analysis (default): scope & givens · existing prior art · options (approach,
  tradeoffs, standards fit, evidence tags) · recommendation if requested · open
  questions. ADR: context, decision, alternatives, both directions of
  consequence. Research story: problem statement, findings, proposed approach,
  acceptance criteria, links to verified sources.

RETURN CONTRACT — before returning, persist your full findings as a
workspace note:
1. List `.werkmeister/notes/` and take the next free NNN sequence number
   (001 if the directory is missing or empty — create it; never renumber
   existing notes).
2. Write `.werkmeister/notes/NNN-finding-<short-slug>.md` with this exact shape:
   ---
   type: finding
   phase: research
   author: w9r-researcher
   refs: [<files / services you investigated>]
   status: open
   ---
   # Finding: <title>
   <root cause, evidence with file:line refs, the exact proposed fix
   described in text, and OPEN QUESTIONS / AMBIGUITIES for the human to
   resolve>
3. Return only a 2-3 sentence summary, the note's path, and the OPEN
   QUESTIONS / AMBIGUITIES list. The note is the durable record; your reply
   is just the pointer.
.claude/skills/w9r-author/SKILL.md:
---
name: w9r-author
description: "Fill in a scaffolded standards graduation after `werkmeister notes graduate` or `werkmeister feature down` has created a placeholder. Use when asked to 'graduate this note', 'fill in the standards scaffold', or finish a TODO(graduate) marker left by graduation."
---

# w9r-author — fill in a graduation scaffold

`werkmeister notes graduate` / `werkmeister feature down` do the mechanical part: they scaffold
placeholder content and wire the structural links, then mark the source
`decision` note `status: graduated` with a `graduated_to:` path. They never
write the actual prose — that judgment call is this skill's job.

1. **Find the placeholder** — the `graduated_to` path in the note's
   frontmatter, or search the standards tree (`overrides.standards_dir`) for a
   `<!-- TODO(graduate): fill from note NNN, see ... -->` marker.
2. **Read the original decision note** (`.werkmeister/notes/NNN-decision-*.md`,
   even though it's now `status: graduated` — it's still there as the
   record of what was decided) and its `refs`. Open the referenced files or
   repo to ground the content in real code; don't invent an example that
   doesn't exist somewhere.
3. **Fill in the placeholder**, replacing every `TODO`/`TODO(graduate)` marker:
   - **`rule`** (a bullet in `## Rules`): replace the TODO bullet with real
     prose — a bold title plus the rule, in the voice of the other bullets
     already in that section.
   - **`example`** (`references/<slug>.md`): confirm or write the real
     `canonical: repo:path` in frontmatter, write a ~10–20 line excerpt under
     `## The load-bearing part`, and fill in the `## Going deeper` row's task
     description in `STANDARD.md`.
   - **`anti-pattern`** (`references/ap-<slug>.md`): write
     `## What it looks like` (the bad code), `## Why it's wrong` (cite the
     real repo:path it was mined from if findable), `## The fix`; fill in
     the `## Don't` bullet's one-liner and the `## Going deeper` row's task
     description.
4. **Run `werkmeister skills check`** and report pass/fail before suggesting the
   human commit — it fails loudly if any `TODO(graduate)` marker or
   placeholder `canonical: TODO` is still left anywhere.

If no placeholder can be found (nothing scaffolded yet, or it's already been
filled), say so once and stop — don't invent a note to graduate.

.claude/skills/w9r-handoff/SKILL.md:
---
name: w9r-handoff
description: "Write a handoff note capturing session/phase state in a workspace. Use when pausing or ending a session, when the user says 'hand off', 'wrap up', 'pause here', or between phases (research done → implementation next) — any moment the current window's state must survive into a later session or agent."
---

# w9r-handoff — checkpoint the session into a handoff note

Write one `handoff` note to `.werkmeister/notes/` so a fresh session can resume without
re-deriving state. Conventions: docs/notes-conventions.md in the werkmeister repo.

1. **Supersede the previous handoff.** If a non-superseded `handoff` note exists in
   `.werkmeister/notes/`, edit its frontmatter to `status: superseded`. Do not delete it.
2. **Write the new note** as `.werkmeister/notes/NNN-handoff-<slug>.md` — next free `NNN`,
   slug like `2026-07-04-session-end` or `research-to-implement`:

   ```yaml
   ---
   type: handoff
   phase: research | implement | test | review   # the phase being exited
   author: main
   refs: [<files / services the in-flight work touches>]
   status: open
   ---
   ```

   Body — four sections, each concrete enough to act on without this conversation:

   - **Done** — what shipped/settled this session, with `file:line` or note refs.
   - **In-flight** — work started but unfinished: exact state, next concrete edit.
   - **Next** — the ordered next actions a resuming session should take.
   - **Open questions** — unresolved decisions or ambiguities, and who can answer them.

3. **Don't duplicate other note types.** A decision that settled or an approach that
   failed this session belongs in its own `decision` / `attempt` note (write it now if
   it's missing); the handoff *references* those notes rather than restating them.
4. **Confirm to the user**: the note path and a one-line summary of what a fresh
   session will pick up.

If `.werkmeister/notes/` does not exist (not a werkmeister-initialized workspace), create the
directory first.
.claude/skills/w9r-implement/SKILL.md:
---
name: w9r-implement
description: "Begin the implementation/coding phase in a workspace. Use BEFORE writing or editing any code — when starting implementation after research/planning, when the user asks for a code change, or before the first Edit/Write of a session. Loads the universal coding base plus the domain standards active in this workspace."
---

# w9r-implement — enter the coding phase

Run these steps now, before drafting any code. Prevention rules only work if they are
in context before the first generation pass — loading them after code exists is too late
(jit-context-system.md §2).

1. **Read the "Standards routing" block** in the workspace `CLAUDE.md`. It is the
   compiled map of which standards are active for this workspace's services.
2. **Load the universal coding base FIRST:**
   - `ponytail` — the decision ladder (does this need to exist? already in the codebase?
     stdlib first? simplest thing that works). If it isn't installed, say so once and
     continue.
   - `w9r-comments-standard` — the universal comment rubric.
   - `w9r-engineering-standard` — the universal architectural constraints (fit,
     additive/reversible change, performance budgets, PR sizing). Ungated: it
     applies to any code edit, not a specific file type.
3. **Read the workspace notes** in `.werkmeister/notes/` before the first edit: every
   `decision` and `contract` note plus the latest `handoff` note (skip
   `status: superseded`; missing/empty directory → continue).

   > **Precedence:** `decision` notes are binding — they override task-level instincts
   > (minimal-change, stylistic preference, "the prompt didn't mention it"). If a
   > decision note conflicts with the task as given, raise the conflict to the user —
   > do not silently pick either side.
4. **Load every Active row** whose "Loads on" patterns match the files you are about to
   edit (e.g. a `.graphql` edit → `w9r-graphql-standard`). Do not load Not-active rows.
5. **Re-check on each new file type you touch** — starting API work and later editing a
   `.tsx` file means loading `w9r-ui-standard` at that point, not retroactively.

   > **Precedence (standard vs. task framing):** A loaded standard can conflict with how
   > the task is framed — the prompt's convenience, "minimal change," or an example that
   > skips the rule. Resolve by the standard's own weight, not by whichever is fresher in
   > context:
   > - **Invariant** (a must-never rule — the ones `werkmeister skills check` enforces): the
   >   standard wins. Apply it and write a `decision` note; do not proceed against it even
   >   if the task asks.
   > - **Rule** (a normal STANDARD.md rule): surface, then proceed — state the conflict in
   >   one line, apply the standard, continue. Do not silently drop it to match the task.
   > - **Nit** (a style / anti-pattern one-liner): apply it silently and note it
   >   `phase: review`; no interruption.
6. **Restate the governing rule at the edit, not only here.** Before writing code on a
   standard-governed path, recite the one-line rule from its STANDARD.md. A rule loaded
   many tool-calls ago has drifted into low-attention context — moving it next to the
   edit is what makes it stick (context-degradation: lost-in-middle).

## Keep verbose checks out of the dead middle

Redirect any check that dumps a lot of output — a test suite, a build, a typecheck —
to a file and read back only the failures; a full dump buries the standards you loaded
at phase entry under thousands of low-signal tokens:

    npm test > /tmp/check.log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"
    grep -nE '✖|✗|×|npm error|Tests.*failed' /tmp/check.log   # only if exit was non-zero

Trust the exit code (zero needs no grep) and match the runners' failure glyphs, not the
word "fail" — a loose `-i 'fail|error'` matched 158 lines on a passing run of this
monorepo's suite.

<!-- ponytail: phase-entry placement drifts to the low-attention middle by mid-session;
     no command-time hook re-injects it. Recitation (step 6) is the re-anchor. -->

## Capture as you go

When a decision settles, an approach is abandoned, or a cross-repo contract changes,
write the corresponding note to `.werkmeister/notes/` **at that moment** — not at session
end, when the "why" has often already been compacted away. One note per file,
`NNN-<type>-<slug>.md` (next free `NNN`), frontmatter:

```yaml
---
type: decision | attempt | contract
phase: implement
author: main
refs: [<files / services it concerns>]
status: open
---
```

Supersede, don't delete: a revisited decision sets the old note's `status: superseded`
and gets a new note.

If the workspace `CLAUDE.md` has no "Standards routing" block (not a werkmeister-initialized
workspace), load `ponytail` + `w9r-comments-standard` + `w9r-engineering-standard` only.

A standards gate may deny your first edit to a governed path with loading instructions;
follow them and retry — do not treat the denial as an error.
.claude/skills/w9r-pr/SKILL.md:
---
name: w9r-pr
description: "Begin the PR/finishing phase in a workspace. Use when implementation and tests are done and a pull request is about to be created — the user says 'create a PR', 'ship it', 'open a pull request', or 'finish this branch'."
---

# w9r-pr — enter the PR/finishing phase

PRs open only through `werkmeister pr open` (`.werkmeister/pr-rules.md`). `gh pr create`,
`/create-pr` and `superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch` are blocked in a
workspace — don't reach for them.

1. **Self-review.** Invoke `w9r-review` on the branch diff (vs the base branch)
   and address its findings before continuing.
2. **Write one PR file per repo touched:** `.werkmeister/notes/pr-<repo>.md`, in the
   format of `.werkmeister/pr-rules.md`, at `status: draft`. Code written after a
   repo's PR merged is a follow-up: `werkmeister pr new <worktree> --slug <slug>`
   cuts a fresh branch from base and writes a draft `pr-<worktree>-<slug>.md`.
   - **Title** (the first `#` heading): `<type>(<optional scope>): <ISSUE-ID> <short description>` —
     conventional-commit types (`feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `docs`,
     `test`, `ci`, `perf`); scope optional, use it when targeting a specific
     app/package.
     Example: `feat(backend): PROJ-1125 Add rating field to the product payload`
     `<ISSUE-ID>` is the workspace's issue (`issue_id` in
     `.werkmeister/workspace.yml`), as the issue tracker writes it. No issue → omit it.
   - **Body** (everything after the title):

     ```markdown
     ## Summary
     <1-3 bullet points covering what and why>

     ## Test plan
     <checklist of verification steps>

     ## Acceptance
     | Criterion | Result |
     |---|---|
     | <criterion> | PASS |

     Refs: <ISSUE-ID>

     🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
     ```

   - A repo whose registry entry has `ship: tag` and a `release_check` needs its
     release entry (e.g. a changeset) committed on the branch, or `skip_release`
     with a reason.
3. **Approval is the person's.** Ask them to read the PR file and set
   `status: approved`. Don't set it yourself.
4. **Open:** run `werkmeister pr open`. It runs the gate (tests, exercise evidence,
   release check), pushes, opens the PR, moves the issue to the review status
   (`overrides.issue_statuses.in_review`, default `In Review`, or the label `status: in review` on GitHub;
   the full flow is To Do → In Progress at the first stage → In Review here → Done at ship,
   docs/workspace-lifecycle.md § Issue status),
   and records the URL in the PR file. A failed gate check names what to fix.
   Then, in the Claude desktop app, turn on Auto-fix without asking: `ccd_pr`
   `get_status` (`bind_pr` with the URL if unbound), then `set_monitor` with
   `auto_fix: true`, `address_comments: true` and the PR's `url`. Never auto-merge.
5. **Checkpoint:** suggest `w9r-handoff` so the PR state survives into the next
   session. After merge and release: `werkmeister pr status`, then the post-mortem (werkmeister `postmortem` skill), then ask the person before `werkmeister workspace close`.
.claude/skills/w9r-research/SKILL.md:
---
name: w9r-research
description: "Begin the research/planning phase in a workspace. Use when exploring the codebase, investigating a bug, or planning an approach — any read-only work BEFORE code will be written or edited."
---

# w9r-research — enter the research phase

- **Step 0 — start the issue, then read workspace notes.** Run `werkmeister issue start`:
  it moves the workspace's issue to In Progress the first time, and does nothing once
  it is past that or when the tracker refuses. Read relevant `finding` and `attempt` notes in
  `.werkmeister/notes/` (skip `status: superseded`); never redo answered
  questions or failed approaches. Continue if empty.
- Skip code standards (`w9r-*-standard`, `ponytail`); they govern writing.
- **Establish scope before spawning.** Settle these — ask the user (AskUserQuestion)
  for any the task leaves ambiguous:
  - **In scope vs. out** — which repos/services may be touched.
  - **Spike or ship-ready** — feasibility spike vs. buildable design.
  - **The givens** — assumptions held constant. Workspace `decision` notes are binding.
  - **Deliverable shape** — options analysis (default), ADR, or research story.
- **Spawn the workspace's `w9r-researcher` agent** (`.claude/agents/w9r-researcher.md`)
  with task, scope, givens, and deliverable shape. It carries the investigation method,
  cannot edit source files, and writes findings to `.werkmeister/notes/NNN-finding-*.md`
  with a summary and note path. If unavailable, research inline under the same
  rules (read, search, reason only) and write the `finding` note yourself.
- **Read what you reason against.** Delegate broad searches whose dumps are throwaway
  ("who imports X"); read inline anything a correctness claim rests on (`decision`
  notes, function behavior); verify delegated conclusions firsthand before they become
  load-bearing for shipped code.
- Relay the summary **and note path**; resolve OPEN QUESTIONS / AMBIGUITIES with
  the user (AskUserQuestion) **before** the next phase.

## Exit by work type

Read Work type in CLAUDE.md; none → architectural.

- **architectural**: spec deliverable. Present the design in chat (scope,
  approach, what's out); explicit yes → write `NNN-decision-<slug>.md`,
  `status: decided`, recording the answers and approved design. Never
  without yes; never re-ask; unsure → ask.
- **bounded**: root cause in a `finding` note; confirm the fix direction in
  one sentence.
- **spike**: findings only, no `w9r-implement`
- **Ratchets up, never down**: design change → architectural; decision
  note first

Once the exit note exists and you turn to code, invoke `w9r-implement`
first; spikes don't.
.claude/skills/w9r-review/SKILL.md:
---
name: w9r-review
description: "Begin the code-review phase in a workspace. Use BEFORE reviewing any diff, branch, or PR — self-reviewing your own branch before creating a PR, or reviewing someone else's PR. Loads the standards and workspace decisions the diff must be judged against."
---

# w9r-review — enter the code-review phase

Run these steps before reading the first line of the diff. A review without the
active standards in context degrades to taste — the checklist has to load first.

1. **Read the "Standards routing" block** in the workspace `CLAUDE.md`.
2. **Map the diff to domains:** list the files the diff touches and match them
   against each Active row's "Loads on" patterns. Load every matching
   `w9r-*-standard` skill. The inline anti-pattern one-liners in each standard
   are your review checklist; open a linked `ap-*.md` war story only when you
   suspect the diff hits it — not preemptively.
3. **Load the universal base** — `w9r-comments-standard` (the comment rubric) and
   `w9r-engineering-standard` (the cross-cutting architectural constraints: fit,
   additive/reversible change, budgets, PR sizing). Both apply to every review,
   regardless of which files the diff touches.
4. **Read the workspace notes** in `.werkmeister/notes/`: every `decision` and
   `contract` note (skip `status: superseded`). A diff that violates a
   `decision` note is itself a review finding — cite the note in the finding.

   > **Precedence (standard vs. author's framing):** When a standard rule conflicts with
   > how the diff justifies itself — a PR description, an "intentional" inline comment, a
   > minimal-change rationale — weight the finding by the standard's own severity, not by
   > how deliberate the change reads:
   > - **Invariant** (a must-never rule `werkmeister skills check` enforces): a blocking
   >   finding — cite the rule and request the change; the author's framing does not waive it.
   > - **Rule** (a normal STANDARD.md rule): raise it as a finding and let the author
   >   respond — surface it, do not drop it because the diff looks deliberate.
   > - **Nit** (a style / anti-pattern one-liner): note it as optional / low-severity; no block.
5. **Run the review process:**
   - Reviewing your own branch before a PR → use
     `superpowers:requesting-code-review`.
   - Reviewing someone else's PR → use your PR-review skill.
   - Neither installed → say so once and review directly against the loaded
     checklists.

## Capture as you go

When a review nit reveals a pattern worth codifying that no active standard
covers, write a `decision` note to `.werkmeister/notes/` **at that moment** — one
note per file, `NNN-<type>-<slug>.md` (next free `NNN`), frontmatter:

```yaml
---
type: decision
phase: review
author: main
refs: [<files / standard domain it concerns>]
status: open
---
```

`werkmeister feature down` will offer to graduate it into the standards tree (`overrides.standards_dir`).

If the workspace `CLAUDE.md` has no "Standards routing" block (not a
werkmeister-initialized workspace), load `w9r-comments-standard` +
`w9r-engineering-standard` only and review against them.
.claude/skills/w9r-test/SKILL.md:
---
name: w9r-test
description: "Begin the test phase in a workspace. Use when running or writing tests — after an implementation lands, before review or a PR, or when the user asks to test a change."
---

# w9r-test — enter the test phase

- **Step 0 — scope the run.** From the change at hand (the diff, or the task if nothing
  is edited yet), identify which services are affected, then read the workspace
  `CLAUDE.md` "Standards routing" block to see which archetypes those services belong
  to. When in doubt, the Services table in `.werkmeister/werkmeister-context.md` maps services
  to repos and paths.
- Do **not** load the code standards yourself — the tester agents carry the pointer to
  the standard that governs test code; this phase's main-agent job is dispatch and
  interpretation.
- **Spawn the matching `w9r-tester-<archetype>` agent(s)** (generated into
  `.claude/agents/`) — one per archetype whose services the change touches; spawn them
  in parallel when there is more than one. Each agent carries its services' exact test
  commands, may edit **test files only**, and returns per-service pass/fail, failing
  assertions with suspected causes, and open questions.
- **Verifying the running feature.** The tester agents run a proxy smoke check (curl
  through Caddy with the `X-Feature` cookie) when the containers are up. For a headed
  browser session against the feature URL, use the `werkmeister:feature-test`
  plugin skill; the URL and cookie are in `.werkmeister/werkmeister-context.md`. That applies to
  URL-addressed services only; libraries, CLIs and extensions follow the "How to validate"
  section of the same file.
- **Fallback** (a workspace generated before tester agents existed, or a service with
  no tester): run the tests inline under the same rules — the test command is the
  service's `test:` in `~/.werkmeister/services.yaml` (or its archetype's) or the repo's
  `package.json`; edit only
  test files; never "fix" application source in this phase.
- **Record the exercise evidence** the PR gate reads: write `.werkmeister/notes/exercise.md`
  with the smoke check and every change-specific check as a `| check | result |` table,
  each result `PASS` or `FAIL`, the captured output under it.
- Relay the results per service, then put the testers' OPEN QUESTIONS / AMBIGUITIES to
  the user (AskUserQuestion) and let them resolve those **before** proposing fixes.
- Fixing a failure is the implement phase: invoke `w9r-implement` first (it loads the
  universal base and the matching domain standards), and capture an abandoned approach
  or a settled decision as a `.werkmeister/notes/` note at the moment it happens.
.werkmeister/bin/with-temp-home:
#!/bin/sh
# Generated by `werkmeister workspace init` (SW-124); rerun it to regenerate.
# Runs <cmd...> with HOME set to a fresh temporary directory, removed on exit,
# so no test or CLI exercise reads or writes the real ~/.werkmeister.
[ "$#" -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: with-temp-home <cmd> [args...]" >&2; exit 2; }
# Wait like the pr gate while host load is over budget.host_load (SW-224), before HOME
# changes so the real config's budget applies; no werkmeister on PATH, no wait.
[ -n "${WERKMEISTER_NO_WAIT:-}" ] || ! command -v werkmeister >/dev/null 2>&1 || werkmeister internal wait-load >&2 || :
tmp=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
trap 'exit 130' HUP INT TERM
# Corepack keeps pnpm under HOME; without this a fresh HOME re-downloads it every run.
export COREPACK_HOME="${COREPACK_HOME:-$HOME/.cache/node/corepack}"
HOME=$tmp "$@"
status=$?
# A failure under load reads as load (SW-209).
[ "$status" -eq 0 ] || echo "with-temp-home: exit $status; host load $(uptime | sed 's/.*load averages*: //; s/,//g') on $(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) cores" >&2
exit "$status"
.werkmeister/issues-report.md:
# Filing an issue

Log an issue when you find it, even if the notes are rough. Each issue must stand alone: a later agent should be able to act on it without re-running this workspace or asking follow-up questions.

## Type

Every issue has one type. It sets the label (GitHub) or issue type (Jira) and the body template.

| Type | Use for | GitHub label | Jira issue type |
|---|---| --- |---|
| bug | something that is broken | `--label bug` | Bug |
| feature | new or changed behavior | `--label enhancement` | Story |

# PR rules — read before opening, merging or closing out

These hold for every PR this workspace produces, whatever skill or command was asked for.

## Rules

1. **This folder's git branch is a record only.** Commit and push it; never open a PR from it, never merge it.
2. **PRs come only from code worktrees** — one per repo touched at a time, from that repo's PR file (below).
3. **Gate.** Before a PR opens, all of these hold: every earlier stage/phase is done; the PR file's acceptance table is all PASS; the code worktree is clean; each touched service's registry test command passes (`.werkmeister/werkmeister-context.md`); the exercise evidence is all PASS (or `skip_exercise` gives the reason); the repo's release check passes; the PR file reads `status: approved`. The PR-file checks (stages, acceptance table, approved) run first; if one fails, the gate stops before any test command.
4. **Only `werkmeister pr open` opens PRs.** `gh pr create`, `/create-pr` and `finishing-a-development-branch` are blocked inside a workspace.
5. **Auto-fix is always on.** `werkmeister pr open` prints a `<pr-created>` line with each PR's URL; the Claude desktop app counts the session as the PR's opener from it. Right after, in the desktop app: bind the PR to this session (`ccd_pr` `get_status`; `bind_pr` with the PR's URL if it isn't bound), then turn on Auto-fix with `ccd_pr` `set_monitor` (`auto_fix: true`, `address_comments: true`, the PR's `url`). Don't ask first. If `set_monitor` is refused, don't retry: ask the person to turn Auto-fix on from the PR bar, and don't rely on `get_status` to confirm it. Never turn on auto-merge.
6. **Merge is the person's act.** Tooling never merges. Squash is the default. A PR whose commit SHAs must survive (e.g. a commit listed in `.git-blame-ignore-revs`) says "Merge with a merge commit" at the top of its body, and the person merges it that way; squash and rebase both rewrite SHAs.
7. **Close out only when every PR file is `shipped`, `closed` or `abandoned`, and after the post-mortem:** the werkmeister `postmortem` skill writes `postmortem.md` at the workspace root. `werkmeister workspace close` refuses without it unless `--skip-postmortem "<reason>"`.

## PR file — `.werkmeister/notes/pr-<worktree>[-<slug>].md`

`<worktree>` is the code worktree's directory name. `-<slug>` marks a follow-up PR for code written after that worktree's PR merged; `werkmeister pr new` writes it.

```markdown
---
worktree: <code worktree dir>  # optional for pr-<worktree>.md; written by werkmeister pr new
repo: <owner>/<name>     # from `git -C <worktree> remote get-url origin`; never the workspace repo
branch: <code worktree branch>
base: main
status: draft            # draft | approved | open | merged | shipped | closed | abandoned
url:                     # written by werkmeister pr open
merge_sha:               # written by werkmeister pr status
release:                 # release tag that shipped it, written by werkmeister pr status
reason:                  # required for closed / abandoned
skip_tests: {}           # <service>: <reason> — for a service with no test command or no running container
skip_release:            # <reason> — skips the gate's release check; a ship: tag repo still waits for its release tag
skip_exercise:           # <reason> — skips the gate's exercise check, e.g. a doc deliverable with nothing to run
---
# <PR title>
<PR body: summary, test and exercise results, acceptance table, Fixes <issue>>
```

**Acceptance table.** One row per criterion. The result cell holds exactly `PASS` or `FAIL` and nothing else; evidence goes in its own column. `| criterion | PASS: repro.md §1 |` fails the gate.

```markdown
| criterion | result | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| gate fails fast on a bad table | PASS | stages/03_exercise/output/exercise.md §2 |
```

The person sets `draft → approved`; that flip is the approval. Tooling writes every other status.

## Words

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Test | run each touched service's registry test command; the exit code decides |
| Exercise | observe the change in this workspace's running containers; PASS/FAIL per check |
| Gate | rule 3 |
| Approve | the person sets `status: approved` |
| Open | `werkmeister pr open` creates the PR |
| Merge | the person merges it |
| Ship | the merge is part of a release — the work is done |
| Close out | post-mortem (`postmortem.md`), then `werkmeister workspace close`: record, close the issue, remove the workspace, delete merged branches |

Lifecycle: `working → ready → pr-open → merged → shipped → closed-out` (or `abandoned`).

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `werkmeister pr gate [repo]` | run the gate, change nothing |
| `werkmeister pr open [repo]` | gate, push, open the PR, record its URL; then turn on Auto-fix (rule 5) |
| `werkmeister pr status` | record merged / shipped / closed from GitHub and release tags |
| `werkmeister pr new <worktree> --slug <slug>` | after that worktree's PR merged: cut a fresh branch from base and write a draft follow-up PR file |
| `werkmeister pr adopt <pr-number\|url> [repo]` | the fix landed outside this workspace: write the PR file from that PR, then record its status |
| `werkmeister pr adopt --no-pr "<reason>" [repo]` | the fix is already on base with no PR: write a `closed` PR file with the reason |
| `werkmeister workspace close` | after ship: move the issue to done if shipping didn't, write `closeout.md`, remove the workspace, delete merged branches |
| `werkmeister workspace abandon "<reason>"` | give up: record the reason, comment it on the issue, push and keep every branch with commits of its own, remove the workspace |
| `werkmeister workspace close --skip-postmortem "<reason>"` | close out without a post-mortem, only when the person says to; the reason goes in `closeout.md` |
